newsitem.title: UK: IPE GAS OIL SEEN UP AHEAD OF EXPIRY, BRENT STEADY.
newsitem.headline: IPE GAS OIL SEEN UP AHEAD OF EXPIRY, BRENT STEADY.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures are expected to open firmer on Tuesday but the expiry of the August contract at midday could make for a choppy session, brokers said.
Brent crude, meanwhile, should begin the day unchanged to five cents firmer, they said.
"We're going for 50 cents to $1 higher on gas oil but all eyes will be on the expiry," said a broker.
"It looks like it could be quite a small position but there is talk that a large player may be looking to take a chunk at delivery," he added.
Aug gas oil settled at $168.00 a tonne on Monday.
Sept Brent settled up 10 cents at $18.58 a barrel and looked set for another session of consolidation following last week's sharp slide in anticipation of a resumption in Iraqi exports.
The first barrels of Kirkuk Blend are expected to start flowing onto tankers at the Turkish port of Ceyhan on Tuesday, but brokers said the outright price largely reflected the news.
Markets would be more interested in how U.S. products perform later in the day and the release of last week's inventory data in the U.S. after the close.
"(NYMEX) gasoline looked weak yesterday and it will be interesting to see whether it continues today," said a broker.
"Gasoline remains a major influence and we keep a close eye on volatility here as preparation is negative and the season heads towards its close," said MeesPierson in a daily report.
On gas oil, some brokers said the Aug/Sept intermonth spread could narrow as the expiry approaches, helped by light shortcovering on the prompt month.
Resistance on the Sept contract was pegged at $170-$171 a tonne.
